questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act of 1773:
1. It made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal, assisted by a council of four members.
2. It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta.
3. It made the Governors of Bombay and Madras independent of the Governor-General of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act created the post of Governor-General of Bengal with a four-member council and set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774. It made Bombay and Madras subordinate to Bengal in matters of war and peace, not independent.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Historical Background

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble:
1. In the Berubari Union case the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution.
2. In the Kesavananda Bharati case the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
3. The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added by the 44th Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Berubari (1960) denied that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and Kesavananda (1973) reversed that view. The three words were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, not the 44th.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Preamble
questions.h: Berubari said no; Kesavananda said yes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about citizenship in India:
1. Articles 5 to 11 in Part II of the Constitution deal with citizenship.
2. The Citizenship Act, 1955 provides for acquisition of citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory.
3. Parliament has the power under Article 11 to make laws on the acquisition and termination of citizenship.
4. Overseas Citizen of India status amounts to dual citizenship under the Constitution.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The first three statements are correct. The Constitution does not permit dual citizenship, and OCI status gives certain rights but is not citizenship.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Citizenship

questions.q:
Match the following Articles of the Constitution with their subjects.
A. Article 50  B. Article 43A  C. Article 39A  D. Article 47
1. Equal justice and free legal aid
2. Separation of judiciary from the executive
3. Participation of workers in management of industries
4. Raising the level of nutrition and public health
questions.e: Article 50 separates the judiciary from the executive, Article 43A (added by the 42nd Amendment) provides for worker participation in management, Article 39A for free legal aid, and Article 47 for nutrition and public health.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about emergency provisions and Fundamental Rights:
1. Under Article 359 the President can suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency.
2. The right to move courts for enforcing Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during a National Emergency.
3. Article 19 is automatically suspended when a National Emergency is declared on the ground of armed rebellion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 359 allows suspension of enforcement of Fundamental Rights, but the 44th Amendment protects Articles 20 and 21 from it. Article 19 is suspended automatically only when the Emergency is on the ground of war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Emergency Provisions and Fundamental Rights

questions.q:
Statement-I: An amendment of the Constitution under Article 368 requires a special majority of Parliament and cannot be initiated in a State Legislature.
Statement-II: Parliament can amend any provision of the Constitution, including its basic structure.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 368 amendments can be initiated only in Parliament, by a special majority. After Kesavananda Bharati (1973) Parliament cannot alter the basic structure, so Statement-II is incorrect.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Amendment of the Constitution; Basic Structure

questions.q:
Which of the following are included in the electoral college for the election of the President of India?
1. Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and of Delhi and Puducherry
2. Nominated members of Parliament
3. Elected members of the Legislative Councils of the States
4. Elected members of both Houses of Parliament
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The electoral college under Article 54 has the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies, including Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils do not vote.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, President of India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a Money Bill:
1. It can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha with the recommendation of the President.
2. The Rajya Sabha must return it to the Lok Sabha within 14 days with or without recommendations.
3. The decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha has 14 days to return it, and the Speaker's certificate on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Parliament

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A judge of the Supreme Court holds office until the age of 65.
2. A judge of a High Court holds office until the age of 65.
3. A Supreme Court judge can be removed by the President only after an address by each House of Parliament, supported by a special majority, on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Supreme Court judges retire at 65 and High Court judges at 62. Removal needs a special majority address in both Houses on proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court and High Court
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Panchayati Raj:
1. The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects for Panchayats.
2. Elections to Panchayats are conducted by the Election Commission of India.
3. Seats in every Panchayat are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects, and reserved seats for SCs and STs in proportion to population. Panchayat elections are conducted by the State Election Commission under Article 243K.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Panchayati Raj

questions.q:
Arrange the following trading companies in the order of their establishment:
1. Dutch East India Company
2. English East India Company
3. French East India Company
4. Danish East India Company
questions.e: The English Company was chartered in 1600, the Dutch in 1602, the Danish in 1616 and the French in 1664.
questions.s: Spectrum, Advent of Europeans in India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Battle of Plassey in 1757 was fought between the English East India Company and Mir Qasim.
2. In the Battle of Buxar in 1764 the English defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II.
3. By the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) the Company obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa from Shah Alam II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Plassey was fought against Siraj-ud-Daulah, not Mir Qasim, who was the Nawab at the time of Buxar. After Buxar the Treaty of Allahabad gave the Company the Diwani, which meant the right to collect revenue.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q: Which one of the following was the first Indian state to accept the Subsidiary Alliance system of Lord Wellesley?
questions.e: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted it in 1798. Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh and the Peshwa (Treaty of Bassein, 1802) followed in the next few years.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q:
Match the following Acts with their provisions.
A. Pitt's India Act, 1784  B. Charter Act, 1813  C. Charter Act, 1833  D. Charter Act, 1853
1. Board of Control to supervise the Company's political affairs
2. Ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and trade with China
3. Created the Governor-General of India and ended the Company's commercial functions
4. Introduced open competition for the civil service
questions.e: Pitt's India Act set up the Board of Control. The 1813 Act ended the monopoly except tea and China, the 1833 Act made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, and the 1853 Act opened civil services to competition.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Historical Background; Spectrum

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sati was declared illegal in 1829 during the tenure of Lord William Bentinck.
2. The first railway line in India, from Bombay to Thane, was opened in 1853 during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie.
3. The Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced by Lord Wellesley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bentinck abolished sati in 1829 and Dalhousie saw the first railway in 1853. The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
questions.s: Spectrum, Governor-Generals and Viceroys

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Santhal rebellion (1855-56) : Sidhu and Kanhu
2. Munda Ulgulan : Kol uprising of Chotanagpur
3. Indigo revolt (1859-60) : Bengal
4. Deccan riots (1875) : Bihar
How many of the pairs given above are correct?
questions.e: The Santhal leaders were Sidhu and Kanhu, and the indigo revolt began in Bengal. The Munda Ulgulan was led by Birsa Munda (1899-1900), distinct from the earlier Kol uprising, and the Deccan riots occurred in Maharashtra.
questions.s: Spectrum, Peasant Movements and Tribal Uprisings

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Revolt of 1857 did not become a nationwide uprising.
Statement-II: Large parts of the country, including Punjab, Bengal and the south, stayed largely unaffected, and rulers such as Scindia, Holkar and the Nizam supported the British.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The revolt was concentrated in north and central India. Where regions stayed quiet and big princely rulers sided with the British, the Company could use their resources and troops against the rebels, which explains why it stayed regional.
questions.s: Spectrum, Revolt of 1857

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828.
2. The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873.
3. The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Ramakrishna Paramahansa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Brahmo Samaj dates from 1828 and the Satyashodhak Samaj from 1873. The Ramakrishna Mission was founded in 1897 by Swami Vivekananda, a disciple of Ramakrishna.
questions.s: Spectrum, Socio-Religious Reform Movements

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's early satyagrahas in India:
1. The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was against the tinkathia system under which peasants had to grow indigo.
2. In the Ahmedabad mill strike of 1918 Gandhi undertook a fast to strengthen the workers' resolve.
3. The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was against the compulsory cultivation of indigo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Champaran concerned the tinkathia system, and Gandhi fasted in Ahmedabad when the workers weakened. Kheda in Gujarat was about remission of revenue after crop failure, not indigo.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence; Spectrum

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ashokan inscriptions:
1. James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in which most Ashokan inscriptions are written.
2. In the north-west, some Ashokan inscriptions were written in Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic.
3. All Ashokan inscriptions are written in the Sanskrit language.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837, and the north-western edicts used Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic. The edicts were written in Prakrit, not Sanskrit.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Themes in Indian History I; Nitin Singhania, Art and Culture

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of the Earth's atmosphere:
1. The early atmosphere, rich in hydrogen and helium, was lost largely under the solar wind.
2. Degassing from the Earth's interior released water vapour, nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
3. The first free oxygen in the atmosphere came directly from volcanic eruptions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Early light gases were blown away by the solar wind, and degassing built a new atmosphere. The build-up of free oxygen came mainly from photosynthesis by early organisms, not from volcanoes.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 2

questions.q:
Match the metamorphic rocks with their parent rocks.
A. Marble  B. Slate  C. Quartzite  D. Gneiss
1. Shale  2. Sandstone  3. Limestone  4. Granite
questions.e: Heat and pressure change limestone to marble, shale to slate, sandstone to quartzite and granite to gneiss.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 5

questions.q:
Statement-I: Temperature generally falls with increasing height in the troposphere.
Statement-II: The troposphere is heated mainly from below by terrestrial radiation and conduction from the Earth's surface rather than directly by incoming solar radiation.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Air is largely transparent to sunlight and is warmed by heat re-radiated from the ground. Layers farther from the surface receive less of that heat, so temperature falls with height.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 8

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs consists of cold ocean currents only?
questions.e: Canary (off north-west Africa) and California are cold currents flowing toward the equator along eastern ocean margins. Kuroshio, Agulhas and Brazil are warm, while Benguela, Falkland and Peru are cold.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 14; Certificate Physical Geography

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Himalayas:
1. The Himadri (Greater Himalaya) is the northernmost and highest range of the Himalayas.
2. The Pir Panjal range belongs to the Shiwaliks.
3. Duns such as Dehradun are longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Himadri is the highest range and the duns lie between the Lesser Himalaya and Shiwaliks. Pir Panjal is the longest range of the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal), not of the Shiwaliks.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian rivers:
1. The Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea through rift valleys and form estuaries.
2. The Godavari is the longest river of the Peninsular plateau.
3. The Krishna is the longest east-flowing river of the Peninsula.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both western-flowing rivers drain through rift valleys and form estuaries. The Godavari, not the Krishna, is the longest east-flowing peninsular river and the longest in the plateau.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian soils:
1. Black soil retains moisture and develops deep cracks when it dries.
2. Black soil is deficient in potash.
3. Laterite soil forms in regions of high temperature and heavy rainfall, where intense leaching occurs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Black (regur) soil holds moisture and cracks on drying. It is rich in lime, potash, iron and magnesium but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross National Product equals Gross Domestic Product plus net factor income from abroad.
2. Net National Product at market prices equals Gross National Product minus depreciation.
3. Gross Domestic Product at factor cost equals GDP at market prices plus net indirect taxes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GNP adds net factor income from abroad to GDP, and subtracting depreciation gives NNP. GDP at factor cost equals GDP at market prices minus net indirect taxes (indirect taxes less subsidies).
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: National Income

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Human Development Report is published by the United Nations Development Programme.
2. The Human Development Index uses gross national income per capita as its income indicator.
3. The Global Hunger Index is published by the United Nations Development Programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UNDP publishes the HDR, and the HDI combines health, education and income (GNI per capita). The Global Hunger Index is produced by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: Growth and Development

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings.
2. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
3. Revenue deficit arises when revenue receipts exceed revenue expenditure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fiscal deficit shows the government's borrowing need, and primary deficit removes interest payments from it. A revenue deficit arises when revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipts.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: Public Finance

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about monetary aggregates in India:
1. M1 includes currency with the public and demand deposits with banks.
2. M1 includes savings deposits with post office savings banks.
3. M3 is M1 plus time deposits with banks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: M1 is narrow money: currency, demand deposits and other deposits with the RBI. Post office savings deposits come in only at the M2 level, and M3 adds time deposits to M1.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: Money

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Wholesale Price Index covers primary articles, fuel and power, and manufactured products.
2. The Wholesale Price Index includes services.
3. India's flexible inflation targeting framework under the RBI Act is defined in terms of the Consumer Price Index.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: WPI tracks goods only and leaves out services. The 2016 amendment to the RBI Act made CPI the basis for the inflation target.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: Inflation

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Cash Reserve Ratio is the share of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be kept as cash with the RBI.
2. Banks must maintain the Statutory Liquidity Ratio in the form of cash, gold or approved securities.
3. Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CRR is held with the RBI, while SLR is held by banks themselves in liquid assets. Repo is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks against securities; the rate at which it borrows is the reverse repo rate.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: Banking

questions.q:
Which of the following are Rabi crops?
1. Wheat
2. Mustard
3. Cotton
4. Gram
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Rabi crops are sown in October-December and harvested in March-April, which suits wheat, mustard and gram. Cotton is a Kharif crop sown with the monsoon.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: Agriculture

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's balance of payments:
1. Remittances sent home by Indians working abroad are recorded in the current account.
2. Foreign direct investment is recorded in the current account.
3. Trade deficit is the excess of merchandise imports over merchandise exports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Remittances are secondary income in the current account, and trade deficit is the merchandise gap. FDI is a capital flow recorded in the financial (capital) account.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy: External Sector

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ecological pyramids:
1. The pyramid of energy is always upright.
2. The pyramid of biomass in a pond ecosystem can be inverted.
3. The pyramid of numbers in a tree ecosystem can be inverted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Energy always falls at each trophic level, so its pyramid is never inverted. In a pond, phytoplankton have small standing biomass but reproduce rapidly, and one tree supports many insects, so those pyramids can be inverted.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Ecology; NCERT Class XII Biology, Ecosystem

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of organisms and their role in the nitrogen cycle:
1. Rhizobium : symbiotic nitrogen fixation in legume roots
2. Nitrobacter : oxidation of nitrite to nitrate
3. Azotobacter : denitrification
4. Nitrosomonas : reduction of nitrate to ammonia
How many of the pairs given above are correct?
questions.e: Rhizobium and Nitrobacter are matched correctly. Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen fixer, and Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Ecosystem; Shankar IAS

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about coral reefs:
1. Corals live in symbiosis with microscopic algae called zooxanthellae.
2. Coral bleaching occurs when corals expel their zooxanthellae under stress such as unusually warm water.
3. Coral reefs occur only in the Pacific Ocean.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Zooxanthellae give corals most of their food and colour, and corals lose both when stressed by heat. Reefs occur in the Indian, Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Ecosystems

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about biodiversity hotspots:
1. A hotspot must contain at least 1,500 species of endemic vascular plants.
2. A hotspot must have lost at least 70 percent of its original natural vegetation.
3. The Eastern Ghats are recognised as a biodiversity hotspot in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: These are the two criteria of Norman Myers. India has hotspots in the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar); the Eastern Ghats are not a hotspot.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Biodiversity

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Project Tiger was launched in 1973.
2. Project Elephant was launched in 1992.
3. Project Elephant is administered by the Ministry of Agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Project Tiger started in 1973 and Project Elephant in 1992, and both are schemes of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Biodiversity Conservation

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Biological Diversity Act, 2002:
1. The National Biodiversity Authority is headquartered in Chennai.
2. Biodiversity Management Committees are set up at the level of local bodies.
3. The National Biodiversity Authority functions under the Ministry of Agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act created the NBA at Chennai, State Biodiversity Boards and local Biodiversity Management Committees. The NBA is a statutory body linked to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Environmental Acts

questions.q:
Statement-I: Carbon monoxide is highly poisonous to humans.
Statement-II: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin with a much greater affinity than oxygen, reducing the blood's capacity to carry oxygen.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Carbon monoxide forms carboxyhaemoglobin, which blocks oxygen transport and causes suffocation at the tissue level. Statement-II is the reason for Statement-I.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Environmental Pollution; NCERT Class XI Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Paris Agreement:
1. It was adopted at the 21st Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC in 2015.
2. It aims to hold the rise in global average temperature to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts toward 1.5 degrees Celsius.
3. It sets legally binding emission reduction targets for developed countries only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Agreement was adopted at COP21 in Paris with that temperature goal. It works through nationally determined contributions from all parties; binding targets for developed countries only was the Kyoto Protocol approach.
questions.s: Shankar IAS, Climate Change

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The sky appears blue because air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths of sunlight more strongly than longer wavelengths.
2. The Sun looks reddish at sunrise and sunset because its light travels a longer path through the atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue light.
3. Rayleigh scattering is stronger for longer wavelengths than for shorter wavelengths.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rayleigh scattering varies inversely with the fourth power of wavelength, so blue scatters far more than red. Statement 3 states it backwards.
questions.s: NCERT Class X Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chandrayaan-3 was launched on the LVM3 launch vehicle.
2. PSLV-C37 placed 104 satellites in orbit in a single mission in 2017.
3. The Mars Orbiter Mission was launched on a GSLV.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LVM3, earlier called GSLV Mk III, carried Chandrayaan-3 in July 2023, and PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites in February 2017. The Mars Orbiter Mission was launched in 2013 on PSLV-C25.
questions.s: ISRO official website

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's three-stage nuclear power programme:
1. The first stage uses pressurised heavy water reactors fuelled by natural uranium.
2. The second stage uses fast breeder reactors with plutonium-based fuel.
3. The third stage is based on uranium-235 as the main fuel.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Homi Bhabha's plan moves from natural uranium PHWRs to plutonium-fuelled fast breeders and then to thorium-based reactors using uranium-233. This is designed to use India's large thorium reserves.
questions.s: DAE; standard S&T notes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about CRISPR-Cas9:
1. It uses a guide RNA to direct the Cas9 enzyme to a specific DNA sequence.
2. The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020 was awarded to Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna for developing it.
3. Cas9 is an enzyme that synthesises RNA from a DNA template.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Guide RNA finds the target and Cas9 cuts the DNA there, allowing edits. Cas9 is a nuclease that cuts DNA; it does not make RNA.
questions.s: Standard S&T notes on biotechnology; Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020

questions.q:
Match the Indian missiles with their types.
A. Akash  B. Astra  C. Nag  D. BrahMos
1. Anti-tank guided missile
2. Beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile
3. Surface-to-air missile
4. Supersonic cruise missile
questions.e: Akash is a surface-to-air missile, Astra a beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, Nag an anti-tank guided missile and BrahMos a supersonic cruise missile developed with Russia.
questions.s: DRDO official website

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about intellectual property in India:
1. A patent is granted for 20 years from the date of filing.
2. Copyright in a literary work lasts for the lifetime of the author plus 60 years.
3. Registration of a geographical indication is valid in perpetuity without any renewal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Patents Act gives a 20-year term, and the Copyright Act gives life plus 60 years. A GI registration is valid for 10 years and can be renewed.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh / DPIIT, IPR notes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice.
2. The Nobel Prize in Physics 2010 was awarded for experiments on graphene.
3. One nanometre is equal to one millionth of a metre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Geim and Novoselov won the 2010 Nobel Prize for graphene. One nanometre is 10^-9 m, a billionth of a metre.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Chemistry; standard S&T notes
